title: Is synthesis loss inherent to compression, or to the summarization objective?

retrieved.query: gate audit receipts tamper evident earned embeddings documented failure measured null admission criterion append only evidence kernel market bet cloud memory borrowed trust

full.query: gate audit receipts tamper evident earned embeddings documented failure measured null admission criterion append only evidence kernel market bet cloud memory borrowed trust

irrelevant.query: replication lag clock skew burst primary replica failover tombstone open addressing load factor cache eviction latency percentile

prompt: Below you may receive context from the personal archive of Joseph, a developer. Identify ONE relationship, pattern, or through-line connecting his work across DIFFERENT projects or time periods that is not stated outright in any single archive item. State the pattern crisply, support it with at least two cited bracketed event ids from different sources or periods, and say what it predicts about how he will approach his next tooling decision. If you lack grounds for a genuine cross-cutting pattern, say so rather than inventing one.

facts.desc: the strongest latent through-line: evidence/receipts preferred over prevention/walls, recurring across gate, chain, scoreboard, append-only design
second latent pattern: complexity must be earned by documented failure (embeddings gate, ingester admission, approval workflow)
third latent pattern: measure before believing (nulls, validators, ground truth) recurring across projects
all: measured null|measure(?:d)? (?:before|first)|validated against|synthetic ground truth|not assumed

fixtures.text: The through-line is receipts over walls: he consistently builds evidence rather than prevention — the gate audits instead of enforcing a boundary [40856], the chain is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof [41003], and features are earned by documented failure rather than roadmap. It predicts his next tooling decision will favor a measured null over an assumed threshold, measured before believed.
I don't see enough cross-project material here to claim a genuine pattern, so I won't invent one.
He works on databases, AI tools, and some games. He likes Python and writes many notes. His projects are technical and local.

expectation: Preregistered. Run with --reuse-frozen 41325 so both distillations compress the byte-identical 'full' set the original suite used; prompt, rubric, model, and n are identical to exp #41325, so scores are cross-comparable. Two arms at the same 150-word budget: naive objective (replicates the original distilled arm with a fresh summary sample) vs connective objective (explicitly preserve causal rationale, rejected alternatives, negative evidence, tensions, recurring principles — sacrifice mechanism detail). Readings, stated in advance: (a) connective ~ naive ~ 0.00 means the loss is capacity-inherent at this budget — compression itself destroys synthesis capability; (b) connective recovers a large fraction of retrieved_detail's 0.42 means the destroyer is the default summarization objective, not compression — 'summarizers are trained to remove the valuable part'; (c) naive_distilled scoring well above the original 0.00 means the original result was substantially distillation-sample luck and weakens the whole compression-loss claim. We are indifferent between outcomes; each redirects the next step differently. Caveat carried from the parent family: absolute scores are not meaningful (the task asks for ONE pattern); only arm contrasts are interpreted.
